1: # Issue tracker
2: 
3: Issues are tracked in **Linear** using the `linctl` CLI.
4: 
5: ## Workflow
6: 
7: Use `linctl` for issue operations in this repo. Do not use GitHub Issues or local `.scratch/` markdown issues unless the repo configuration changes.
8: 
9: Issue identifiers follow the format `DHC-123`.
10: 
11: Use the Linear CLI to create an issue with the appropriate team/project, title, description, and triage label/status.
12: 
13: ```bash
14: linctl issue create --title "Title" --description "Body"
15: ```
16: 
17: ## CLI usage
18: 
19: ```bash
20: linctl issue list
21: ```
22: 
23: ## Viewing an issue
24: 
25: ```bash
26: linctl issue get <issue-id>
27: ```
28: 
29: This installed `linctl` does not provide `issue view`; use `issue get` for issue details.
30: 
31: ## Updating triage state
32: 
33: Apply the matching triage label/status string from `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` using `linctl`.
34: 
35: Repository: `alessandrojcm/dhc-dashboard`
36: 
37: ## Projects & milestones
38: 
39: - Feature tickets may target the `DHC Dashboard` project: `linctl issue create --team ALE --project "DHC Dashboard" ...`, optionally with `--project-milestone <name>` for release grouping (e.g. `v3`).
40: - linctl has no milestone management subcommand. Create milestones via raw GraphQL:
41:   `linctl graphql -q 'mutation { projectMilestoneCreate(input: { projectId: "<project-uuid>", name: "<name>" }) { success projectMilestone { id name } } }'`
42:   Get the project UUID from `linctl project list -j` / `linctl project get`.
43: 
44: ## Wayfinding operations
45: 
46: - Wayfinder maps use `wayfinder:map`; child tickets use exactly one of `wayfinder:research`, `wayfinder:prototype`, `wayfinder:grilling`, or `wayfinder:task`.
47: - Create all map tickets first, then attach each child with `linctl issue update <child> --parent <map>`.
48: - Express blocking with Linear relations: `linctl issue relation add <blocker> --blocks <blocked>`.
49: - The frontier is the map's open, unassigned children whose blocking relations are all closed. Claim one before work with `linctl issue assign <ticket>`.
50: - Verify the map and its children with `linctl issue get <map>`, and inspect dependency edges with `linctl issue relation list <ticket>`.
51: 
52: ## Relation direction gotcha
53: 
54: Agents keep entering `--blocks` relations backwards. The flag points **from the blocker toward the blocked issue**: `linctl issue relation add ALE-A --blocks ALE-B` means **ALE-A must finish before ALE-B** (ALE-A is the prerequisite, ALE-B is the dependent). Equivalently, read it as "ALE-A blocks ALE-B."
55: 
56: When sequencing an expand→code→contract split (e.g. ALE-179), the correct edges are: expand `--blocks` code, and code `--blocks` contract. The expand migration is the frontier, not the contract. Before treating a Linear-reported "unblocked" issue as the frontier, cross-check it against the spec's stated ordering — if Linear's graph disagrees with the spec, the relations are inverted and must be fixed (`relation remove` the wrong edge, then `relation add` the correct one) before claiming the ticket.

1: # Code-Authored Templates Synced to Resend-Hosted Templates
2: 
3: **Status:** Accepted  
4: **Date:** 2026-08-22  
5: **Tags:** email, resend, react-email, templates, ci-cd
6: 
7: ## Context
8: 
9: Loops hosts transactional email templates in its dashboard: content and subject/sender metadata are invisible to the repository, unreviewable, and unauditable by agents. Migrating to Resend is the moment to flip template ownership. Resend offers two send models: dashboard-hosted templates (`template: {id, variables}`) or per-send inline `html`. Resend also supports authoring templates as React Email components and uploading them programmatically (official `resend` CLI; Templates API with stable aliases; draft→publish lifecycle with version history).
10: 
11: ## Decision
12: 
13: Each Email Kind is authored as a React Email component in a new `packages/email-templates` workspace package. The component file also declares its Template metadata — default subject, default sender, declared typed variables (`string | number`, optional fallback) — making TypeScript the single schema authority for what each Kind requires. The Elixir side keeps only its generic string|number validation; Resend enforces per-template variable contracts at send time.
14: 
15: Templates remain hosted at Resend. A sync pipeline renders components to HTML and uploads them via the official CLI/API:
16: 
17: - Pull requests upload drafts only; merging to main publishes. Publishing therefore gates on review plus required checks, never on an arbitrary push.
18: - Templates carry a stable alias derived mechanically from the Email Kind (kebab-case). Sends address `template.id` by that alias, so no kind→ID configuration map or env-var indirection exists at runtime.
19: - Dashboard edits to templates are drift; the next sync overwrites them. Resend's version history is the recovery mechanism.
20: 
21: The cutover from Loops is a single global adapter flip rehearsed against Resend's sandbox in dev (no staging environment exists), with Loops credentials kept warm for instant rollback.
22: 
23: ## Consequences
24: 
25: - Template changes deploy through git review like all other code; agents can read and write templates.
26: - The provider's template store remains part of the production path: a future provider migration must re-upload templates there. Accepted in exchange for hosted rendering, server-side variable interpolation/escaping, and zero rendering machinery in Elixir.
27: - Non-prod environments keep receiving a JSON summary of Kind + data variables in Mailpit rather than rendered HTML; visual previews happen through React Email's local preview server during authoring.
28: - A typo'd alias surfaces as a send-time validation error; mitigated by the compile-time Email Kind whitelist plus a check asserting every whitelisted Kind has a published template.
29: 
30: ## Considered options
31: 
32: - **Recreate templates in Resend's dashboard.** Rejected: closest to today's shape but keeps content invisible to the repo and would be throwaway work once code ownership landed.
33: - **App-shipped HTML** — render artifacts in-repo and send inline `html` per send. Rejected: makes the provider pure transport, but drags placeholder interpolation and HTML escaping into Elixir, ships rendered blobs alongside the Phoenix release, and forfeits Resend's draft/publish/versioning machinery.

(End of file - total 33 lines)
</content>

1: /**
2:  * Template metadata schema for the code-authored transactional email
3:  * templates (ADR 0022 — Code-Authored Templates Synced to Resend-Hosted
4:  * Templates).
5:  *
6:  * Each component file in `emails/` exports its metadata via
7:  * {@link defineTemplate}, making TypeScript the single schema authority for
8:  * what each Email Kind requires: default subject, default sender, and the
9:  * declared typed variables. The Elixir side keeps only its generic
10:  * string|number validation and Resend enforces the per-template variable
11:  * contract at send time.
12:  *
13:  * Constraints encoded here mirror Resend's template rules:
14:  *
15:  * - variable keys are UPPER_SNAKE and referenced as {{{KEY}}} in markup;
16:  * - at most 20 declared variables per template;
17:  * - reserved names cannot be declared.
18:  *
19:  * The fallback/type correlation is expressed statically through the
20:  * {@link TemplateVariable} discriminated union, so an invalid pairing fails
21:  * compilation instead of validation.
22:  */
23: 
24: /** The five whitelisted Email Kinds — mirrors `@transactional_ids` in `Dhc.Email.Worker`. */
25: export const EMAIL_KINDS = [
26:   "inviteMember",
27:   "workshopAnnouncement",
28:   "workshopRegistration",
29:   "workshopRegistrationError",
30:   "magicLink",
31: ] as const;
32: 
33: export type EmailKind = (typeof EMAIL_KINDS)[number];
34: 
35: interface VariableBase {
36:   /** UPPER_SNAKE key as declared on the Resend-hosted template (`{{{KEY}}}`). */
37:   readonly key: string;
38: }
39: 
40: export interface StringTemplateVariable extends VariableBase {
41:   readonly type: "string";
42:   /** Optional fallback rendered when a send omits the variable. */
43:   readonly fallback?: string;
44: }
45: 
46: export interface NumberTemplateVariable extends VariableBase {
47:   readonly type: "number";
48:   readonly fallback?: number;
49: }
50: 
51: export type TemplateVariable = StringTemplateVariable | NumberTemplateVariable;
52: 
53: export type TemplateVariableType = TemplateVariable["type"];
54: 
55: export interface TemplateMetadata {
56:   /** The stable provider-neutral Email Kind (`inviteMember`, …). */
57:   readonly kind: EmailKind;
58:   /** Kebab-case alias derived from the kind; Resend templates are addressed by it. */
59:   readonly alias: string;
60:   readonly subject: string;
61:   /** Default sender in `Name <addr>` form. */
62:   readonly from: string;
63:   readonly variables: readonly TemplateVariable[];
64: }
65: 
66: export interface TemplateDefinition {
67:   kind: EmailKind;
68:   subject: string;
69:   from: string;
70:   variables: readonly TemplateVariable[];
71: }
72: 
73: /** Names Resend reserves on every template; declaring them is an error. */
74: export const RESERVED_VARIABLE_NAMES = new Set([
75:   "FIRST_NAME",
76:   "LAST_NAME",
77:   "EMAIL",
78:   "RESEND_UNSUBSCRIBE_URL",
79:   "contact",
80:   "this",
81: ]);
82: 
83: /** Resend allows at most 20 declared variables per template. */
84: const MAX_VARIABLES = 20;
85: 
86: const UPPER_SNAKE = /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(_[A-Z0-9]+)*$/;
87: const SENDER_WITH_ADDRESS = /<[^<>]+@[^<>]+\.[^<>]+>|^[^\s<]+@[^\s<]+\.[^\s<]+$/;
88: 
89: /**
90:  * Derives the kebab-case template alias of an Email Kind. Sends address the
91:  * Resend-hosted template by this alias, so no kind→ID configuration map ever
92:  * exists at runtime (ADR 0022).
93:  */
94: export function templateAlias(kind: string): string {
95:   return kind.replace(/([a-z0-9])([A-Z])/g, "$1-$2").toLowerCase();
96: }
97: 
98: function validate(definition: TemplateDefinition): void {
99:   const { kind, subject, from, variables } = definition;
100: 
101:   if (subject.trim() === "") {
102:     throw new Error(`Template "${kind}" must declare a non-empty subject`);
103:   }
104: 
105:   if (!SENDER_WITH_ADDRESS.test(from)) {
106:     throw new Error(`Template "${kind}" must declare a "from" sender ("Name <addr>" or "addr")`);
107:   }
108: 
109:   if (variables.length > MAX_VARIABLES) {
110:     throw new Error(
111:       `Template "${kind}" declares ${variables.length} variables; Resend allows at most ${MAX_VARIABLES}`,
112:     );
113:   }
114: 
115:   const seen = new Set<string>();
116: 
117:   for (const { key } of variables) {
118:     if (!UPPER_SNAKE.test(key)) {
119:       throw new Error(
120:         `Template "${kind}" variable "${key}" must be UPPER_SNAKE (e.g. INVITATION_LINK)`,
121:       );
122:     }
123: 
124:     if (RESERVED_VARIABLE_NAMES.has(key.toUpperCase())) {
125:       throw new Error(`Template "${kind}" variable "${key}" is reserved by Resend`);
126:     }
127: 
128:     if (seen.has(key)) {
129:       throw new Error(`Template "${kind}" declares duplicate variable "${key}"`);
130:     }
131:     seen.add(key);
132:   }
133: }
134: 
135: /**
136:  * Declares a template's metadata, validating Resend's constraints eagerly so
137:  * a bad definition fails at import time instead of at send or sync time.
138:  */
139: export function defineTemplate(definition: TemplateDefinition): TemplateMetadata {
140:   validate(definition);
141: 
142:   return Object.freeze({
143:     kind: definition.kind,
144:     alias: templateAlias(definition.kind),
145:     subject: definition.subject,
146:     from: definition.from,
147:     variables: Object.freeze([...definition.variables].map((v) => Object.freeze(v))),
148:   });
149: }

input.prompt:
Research the current (2026) Resend email platform's Templates feature APIs. This is for a CI sync pipeline that renders React Email components to HTML and upserts them as Resend-hosted templates.

I need precise answers on:

1. The official `resend` npm CLI: does it support managing **Templates** (the dashboard-hosted templates feature, NOT sending emails)? List the exact subcommands/syntax if yes (create/update/publish/list/get), including flags like alias, subject, from, html, status/draft vs publish.
2. The Resend REST **Templates API** (api.resend.com): exact endpoints and JSON payloads for:
   - Create a template (draft) — payload fields (name, alias?, subject, from, html, variables?)
   - Update an existing template
   - Publish a template
   - Get a single template by id or alias — response shape (fields like `id`, `alias`, `status`: e.g. "draft"|"published", `name`)
   - List templates — pagination model
3. Whether templates can be addressed by a stable string **alias** at send time (`template: { ... }` param of POST /emails), and whether create/update accepts setting that alias.
4. Any rate limits or gotchas for these endpoints.
5. Environment variable conventions the CLI uses for auth (e.g. RESEND_API_KEY).

Useful starting points: https://resend.com/docs/dashboard/templates/introduction , https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/templates/* , https://resend.com/docs/cli/introduction , the resend npm package docs. Verify against live docs pages rather than memory.

Return: a concise but complete summary with exact endpoint paths, request/response field names, exact CLI command syntax, and source URLs for each claim. If some part is not supported (e.g. CLI lacks template management), say so explicitly so we can fall back to the REST API via curl/fetch.

I have everything I need. Here is the consolidated research summary. --- # Resend Templates — API & CLI Reference (2026) ## 1. The `resend` CLI — Templates subcommand **Yes**, the CLI manages dashboard-hosted Templates. Source: , . ### Subcommands ```bash resend templates create # Create a new template (starts as draft) resend templates list # List all templates resend templates get # Retrieve a template by ID or alias resend templates update resend templates publish # Publish a draft resend templates duplicate resend templates delete resend templates open [id] # Open in the dashboard ``` ### `templates create` flags (documented surface) ```bash resend templates create \ --name "Welcome" \ --subject "Welcome to Acme" \ --html "

Hi {{{NAME}}}

" \ --var PRODUCT:string:item \ --var PRICE:number:25 # OR (mutually exclusive with --html): --react-email ./emails/welcome.tsx ``` Flags explicitly documented for the CLI: `--name`, `--subject`, `--html` / `--react-email`, repeated `--var KEY:TYPE:FALLBACK`. **Not documented as CLI flags**: `--alias`, `--from`, `--reply-to`, `--text`, `--status` (draft/published), or a raw `--variables` JSON. The same restricted flag set applies to `templates update`. **Gotcha for the CI pipeline:** if you need `alias`, `from`, `reply_to`, `text`, or a non-string `fallbackValue`, the CLI's template surface is incomplete — fall back to the REST API (or the Node SDK) for full control. ### CLI authentication (auth precedence, highest first) 1. `--api-key re_xxx` flag on any command 2. `RESEND_API_KEY` environment variable 3. Saved credentials from `resend login [--key re_xxx]` Source: . CI-friendly setup: ```yaml env: RESEND_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.RESEND_API_KEY }} ``` --- ## 2. Resend REST Templates API (`https://api.resend.com`) All requests require `Authorization: Bearer re_xxxxxxxxx` and `Content-Type: application/json`. ### Create a template — `POST /templates` Source: Request body fields: | Field | Type | Required | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | `name` | string | yes | Human-readable name | | `html` | string | yes | HTML body. Variables referenced as `{{{VAR_NAME}}}` (triple-brace Handlebars) | | `from` | string | no | `"Your Name "`. Sets the default sender; can be overridden at send time | | `subject` | string | no | Default subject; overridable at send time | | `reply_to` | string \| string[] | no | Default reply-to; overridable | | `text` | string | no | Plain text body. If omitted, derived from `html`. Empty string opts out | | `alias` | string | no | **Stable string identifier usable at send time** (see §3) | | `variables` | array | no | Up to 50 entries; each `{ key, type, fallback_value }` | | `react` | `React.ReactNode` | no | Node.js SDK only — server-renders to HTML | Created templates are **drafts** by default — they cannot be used to send until published. Source: . ### Update a template — `PATCH /templates/:template_id` *(also shown as `PUT /templates/{id}` in some docs — see gotcha)* Source: . Path param `:template_id` accepts either the template UUID or the alias. All body fields are optional (sparse update): `name`, `html`, `alias`, `from`, `subject`, `reply_to`, `text`, `react`, `variables`. Updates land as **drafts** — they do not affect the live published version until you re-publish. ### Publish a template — `POST /templates/:template_id/publish` Source: . Empty body. Response: ```json { "id": "34a080c9-...", "object": "template" } ``` There is **no documented `unpublish` endpoint** — once published, you continue editing against a draft and re-publish to roll forward. ### Get a template — `GET /templates/:template_id` Path param accepts ID **or alias** (CLI confirms: `resend templates get `). Response fields (assembled from create/publish docs and SDK examples — the official `get-template` API reference is thin; the canonical full shape is what `list` and `create` return): ```json { "id": "d9d69002-6301-4a9e-8317-43717351079f", "name": "Welcome Email", "alias": "welcome-message", "status": "draft", // "draft" | "published" "from": "Acme ", "subject": "Welcome", "html": "

Hi {{{NAME}}}

", "text": "Hi {{NAME}}", "reply_to": ["reply@example.com"], "variables": [ { "key": "NAME", "type": "string", "fallback_value": "friend" } ], "created_at": "2026-10-06 23:47:56.678+00", "updated_at": "2026-10-06 23:47:56.678+00", "published_at": "2026-10-07 10:00:00.000Z" // present when published } ``` (`status` and `published_at` are documented on the publish response and version-history page; `alias` is documented on the list response.) ### List templates — `GET /templates` Source: . Pagination: cursor-based, query params: - `limit` (int, default 50) - `after` (string) — return templates after this template ID - `before` (string) — return templates before this template ID Response envelope: ```json { "object": "list", "data": [ { "id": "...", "name": "...", "alias": "...", "status": "...", "created_at": "...", "updated_at": "..." } ], "has_more": true, "next_cursor": "..." // some pages also return "next_page_token" } ``` (`has_more` + cursor field names vary slightly across doc snippets — `next_cursor` and `next_page_token` both appear.) ### Other endpoints - `DELETE /templates/:template_id` → `{ "id": "..." }` - `POST /templates/:template_id/duplicate` → `{ "id": "...", "name": "Original (Copy)" }` --- ## 3. Sending with an alias at send time **Yes** — `template.id` accepts either the template UUID **or the alias**. Source: , : > "To send an email using a template, provide a `template` object with an `id` (or alias) of the published template and an optional `variables` object." ```jsonc POST https://api.resend.com/emails { "from": "Acme ", "to": "delivered@resend.dev", "template": { "id": "order-confirmation", // <-- works with alias string "variables": { "PRODUCT": "Vintage Macintosh", "PRICE": 499 } } } ``` **Constraints at send time** (worth knowing for CI): - `template` cannot coexist with `html`, `text`, or `react` in the same payload. - Top-level `from`, `subject`, `reply_to` in the send payload **override** the template defaults. - Variable keys must match ASCII letters / digits / underscores only; missing variables with no `fallback_value` cause a validation error. Alias is **settable** on both `POST /templates` (create) and `PATCH /templates/:id` (update) — confirmed by the create-template and update-template reference pages (both list `alias` in the body parameters). --- ## 4. Rate limits & gotchas - **Default rate limit: 5 requests per second per team**, shared across all API keys for the team. Source: . Exceeding returns `429`. - Response headers (IETF draft-6): - `ratelimit-limit`, `ratelimit-remaining`, `ratelimit-reset`, `retry-after` - One older doc snippet also mentions "100 requests per minute per IP" — the **5 req/sec per team** is the current canonical value (rate-limit page); the 100/min/IP phrasing is legacy. - Limits can be raised on request for trusted senders (Settings → Usage page). - **HTTP method inconsistency**: the update-template reference shows `PUT /templates/{id}` while other Resend pages (knowledge-base, dashboard topics) show `PATCH /templates/:template_id`. The Node SDK example uses `resend.templates.update()` (which maps to `PATCH`). For CI, **prefer PATCH** as the safe default and fall back to PUT only if a 405 surfaces in your environment. --- ## 5. Source URLs (everything referenced above) - CLI overview: - CLI auth & `RESEND_API_KEY`: (section "CLI Authentication") - Templates dashboard intro: - Templates draft vs published: - API reference index: , `…/update-template`, `…/publish-template`, `…/list-templates`, `…/delete-template` - Send email (template via alias): , - Rate limits: - Full LLM-readable mirror: --- ## TL;DR for the CI sync pipeline - **CLI works** for create / update / publish / list / get / duplicate / delete, but its flag surface on `templates create`/`update` is narrow: `--name --subject --html|--react-email --var KEY:TYPE:FALLBACK`. No documented `--alias`, `--from`, `--reply-to`, `--text`, or `--status` flags. - **REST API** gives you the full surface: `POST /templates` with `{name, html, from?, subject?, reply_to?, text?, alias?, variables?, react?}`. Edit-as-draft, then `POST /templates/:id/publish`. Update via `PATCH /templates/:id` (alias-acceptable). - **Alias works as a stable send-time address**: `{ template: { id: "", variables: {…} } }` in `POST /emails`. - **Drafts must be published** before `POST /emails` will use them — write/upsert + explicit publish are two separate calls. - **5 req/sec/team** is the cap; respect `retry-after` on 429s. - **Auth:** `RESEND_API_KEY` env var (or `--api-key` flag, or `resend login --key`) — wire it as a CI secret. Given your stated needs (`alias`, `from`, `subject`, `html` from React Email), the cleanest CI path is **Node SDK `resend.templates.create(...)` / `update()` / `publish()`**, falling back to raw `fetch` to `api.resend.com` for anything the CLI can't express — not the CLI itself.

1: # Commands
2: 
3: All tasks are defined in `.mise.toml`. Run `mise tasks` to list them all.
4: 
5: ## Setup
6: 
7: ```bash
8: # First time: install all pinned tools (Node, Erlang, Elixir, pnpm)
9: mise install
10: 
11: # Activate mise in your shell (one-time, add to your shell rc)
12: eval "$(mise activate bash)"    # bash
13: eval "$(mise activate zsh)"     # zsh
14: mise activate fish | source     # fish
15: ```
16: 
17: After activation, `node`, `elixir`, `mix`, `pnpm` etc. resolve to the versions pinned in `.mise.toml` on every `cd`.
18: 
19: ## SvelteKit (`apps/web`)
20: 
21: ```bash
22: # Dev (start in order)
23: docker compose up -d db mailpit   # 1. Start PostgreSQL + Mailpit (dev email catcher)
24: mise run phx-server               # 2. Phoenix API and Oban workers
25: mise run dev                      # 3. SvelteKit dev from apps/web
26: ```
27: 
28: - The SvelteKit dev server serves **HTTPS** at the canonical local origin `https://127.0.0.1:5173` (`vite-plugin-mkcert`, self-signed). Probe it with `curl -sk https://127.0.0.1:5173/...`; plain `http://` curls fail even when the server is up. Keep frontend URLs, redirects, and browser visits on `127.0.0.1` rather than mixing it with `localhost`, because host-only auth cookies do not cross between them.
29: - Phoenix remains on `http://127.0.0.1:4000` in development. Since the browser frontend and API use different schemes, development auth cookies are intentionally `Secure; SameSite=None` and browser API calls use credentialed CORS. E2E remains a separate HTTP-only `127.0.0.1` topology with `SameSite=Lax` cookies.
30: - Unhandled server errors are console-logged (status, method, path, route, stack) by `logUnhandledServerError` in `apps/web/src/hooks.server.ts`, wrapped inside Sentry's `handleError`. The catch-all UI is the root `apps/web/src/routes/+error.svelte` plus `apps/web/src/error.html` (fallback for errors in `handle`, `+server.js`, or the root layout load, which no `+error.svelte` can render).
31: 
32: ```bash
33: 
34: # Testing
35: mise run test-unit          # Vitest
36: mise run test-browser       # Vitest Browser Mode component tests in Chromium
37: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_... mise run test-e2e
38:                             # Playwright + real Stripe test mode; self-starts disposable PostgreSQL, Phoenix, and SvelteKit
39: mise run check              # Svelte type check (NOT raw tsc)
40: 
41: # Lint & format
42: mise run lint               # Oxlint (web Svelte/JS/TS + API client TS)
43: mise run format             # Auto-format with Oxfmt
44: ```
45: 
46: Oxlint runs in `apps/web`, `packages/api-client`, and `packages/email-templates`;
47: the generated API client under `packages/api-client/src/client/` is ignored.
48: Oxfmt covers `apps/web` and `packages/email-templates`.
49: The shared config loads the project-local anti-slop plugin from
50: `tools/oxlint/anti-slop/`; keep `oxlint` and `@oxlint/plugins` on the same pinned
51: version when upgrading it, and leave all anti-slop rules enabled at error severity.
52: 
53: Playwright starts its Phoenix and SvelteKit processes through the internal
54: `e2e-phoenix-server` and `e2e-web-server` mise tasks. Their task-local environment
55: is the source of truth for E2E server settings; do not duplicate those variables
56: in `playwright.config.ts` command strings.

58: ## Dev email catching (Mailpit)
59: 
60: The compose file ships a `mailpit` service (`axllent/mailpit`). In dev, the
61: email worker (`Dhc.Email.Worker`) delivers through Swoosh's Mailpit **HTTP**
62: adapter (ADR 0021): each job arrives as a real message whose body is the
63: pretty-printed JSON summary (recipient, friendly template name, data
64: variables), since only the provider can render the real templates. Web UI at
65: `http://localhost:8025` (override with `MAILPIT_HTTP_URL`; the SMTP port 1025
66: is no longer used). Messages are in-memory and lost on container restart. A
67: stopped Mailpit container is not an error: delivery failures log a warning and
68: the job still succeeds.
69: 
70: The E2E suite intentionally uses Stripe's real test API for invitation acceptance.
71: It fails before startup unless `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` starts with `sk_test_`. The test
72: account must provide active `monthly_membership_fee` and `annual_membership_fee`
73: lookup-key prices; coupon tests create unique promotion fixtures and clean them up.
74: Never supply a live-mode key.
75: 
76: ## Phoenix (in progress)
77: 
78: Phoenix mise tasks override the root Supabase Docker `.env` database host and connect to host-local Supabase Postgres at `localhost:54322`.
79: 
80: ```bash
81: # Setup (first time)
82: mise run phx-setup          # deps.get + ecto.create + ecto.migrate
83: 
84: # Server
85: mise run phx-server         # Start dev server (hot-reload) on :4000
86: mise run phx-console        # Start server inside IEx interactive shell
87: 
88: # Database
89: mise run phx-migrate        # Run pending migrations
90: mise run phx-rollback       # Rollback last migration
91: mise run phx-gen-migration NAME  # Generate a new migration
92: ```
93: 
94: ### One-off Discord roster export and assignment review
95: 
96: Export the existing guild roster once with `@discordjs/rest`, which handles
97: Discord rate limits while the script paginates through the guild. The bot token
98: and guild ID come only from the process environment. The script writes
99: `roster.json` with mode `0600`; keep it restricted and delete it after the
100: migration review window.
101: 
102: ```bash
103: DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=... \
104: DISCORD_GUILD_ID=... \
105: node scripts/discord-roster-export.mjs
106: 
107: # Stage rows are a plain JSON array of
108: # {"principal_id":"...","discord_user_id":"...","username_snapshot":"..."}.
109: # The command prints the generated capture ID used by the later phases.
110: cd apps/phoenix
111: DISCORD_SUBJECT_FINGERPRINT_KEY=... \
112: mix dhc.discord.assignments stage ../../roster.json /secure/path/stage-rows.json PREPARER_PRINCIPAL_ID
113: 
114: # Review displays the selected roster evidence. Apply-review consumes a plain
115: # array of {"assignment_id":"...","decision":"approve|reject"}.
116: mix dhc.discord.assignments review CAPTURE_ID ../../roster.json REVIEWER_PRINCIPAL_ID
117: DISCORD_SUBJECT_FINGERPRINT_KEY=... \
118: mix dhc.discord.assignments apply-review CAPTURE_ID /secure/path/review-rows.json REVIEWER_PRINCIPAL_ID
119: 
120: DISCORD_SUBJECT_FINGERPRINT_KEY=... \
121: mix dhc.discord.assignments report CAPTURE_ID ../../roster.json
122: ```
123: 
124: The separately authenticated operator supplies the preparer and reviewer IDs;
125: the task authorizes both against current Member-admin roles in the database, and
126: they must be different. The ID arguments are not authentication credentials.
127: The roster exporter is throwaway migration tooling, not a recurring sync or
128: Phoenix runtime task.
129: 
130: # Code quality
131: mise run phx-format         # Format all Elixir files
132: mise run phx-format-check   # Check formatting (CI)
133: mise run phx-reach          # Reach architecture policy checks (.reach.exs)
134: mise run phx-precommit      # Full check: credo + reach arch + audit + compile + unlock + format + test
135: 
136: # Testing
137: mise run phx-test           # Run all Phoenix tests (excludes :integration tests)
138: 
139: # For specific test files, run directly:
140: cd apps/phoenix && mix test test/some_test.exs
141: cd apps/phoenix && mix test --failed     # Re-run only failed tests
142: cd apps/phoenix && mix ecto.migrations   # Show migration status
143: 
144: # Integration tests are excluded by default. Run with:
145: cd apps/phoenix && mix test --include integration
146: cd apps/phoenix && mix test test/dhc/stripe_sync/workers/worker_integration_test.exs --include integration
147: 
148: # Stripe sync integration test hits Stripe test mode and creates its own
149: # customers/subscriptions. Required: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY. STRIPE_SYNC_TEST_PRICE_ID
150: # is optional when lookup_key=standard_membership_fee exists in Stripe test mode.
151: cd apps/phoenix && \
152:   STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_... \
153:   STRIPE_SYNC_TEST_PRICE_ID=price_... \
154:   mix test test/dhc/stripe_sync/workers/worker_integration_test.exs --include integration
155: ```
156: 
157: Tests that use `Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.unboxed_run/2` commit outside the
158: per-test sandbox transaction and must explicitly delete every durable fixture
159: in `on_exit/1`. If teardown must remove immutable Discord assignment audit rows,
160: disable only `discord_assignment_reject_audit_mutation` for that deletion and
161: always re-enable it in an `after` block.
162: 
163: ### Reach architecture policy (`apps/phoenix/.reach.exs`)
164: 
165: Reach (`mix reach.check --arch`, also in the `precommit` alias) enforces module-boundary rules Credo cannot express:
166: 
167: - Layers: `DhcWeb.*` / `Dhc.*` / `Dhc.Repo`; domain must not depend on web (except `DhcWeb.Endpoint` infrastructure edges), Repo must not depend on web, and the web layer must not touch the Repo directly (`DhcWeb.Plugs.MagicLinkRateLimit` is the one documented seam).
168: - Forbidden calls: `Dhc.Stripe.Client.request/1` outside the client itself (Stripe goes through generated `Dhc.Stripe.Operations.*`), any `Nostrum.*` outside `Dhc.Discord.*`, `HTTPoison`/`Tesla`/`:httpc` anywhere, and `IO.puts` outside Mix tasks and `Dhc.Release`.
169: 
170: Findings are fingerprinted against `.reach-baseline.json`. New findings fail the build; only baseline a known transitional finding with:
171: 
172: ```bash
173: cd apps/phoenix && MIX_ENV=dev mix reach.check --arch --write-baseline .reach-baseline.json
174: ```
175: 
176: The config pins `checks.source_paths: ["lib"]`, so one baseline stays valid across dev and test environments.
177: 
178: ### Sentry (production error tracking)
179: 
180: Sentry activates automatically when `SENTRY_DSN` env var is set. Inactive otherwise.
181: 
182: ```bash
183: # Enable Sentry (set this in production)
184: export SENTRY_DSN="https://your-dsn@sentry.io/your-project-id"
185: ```
186: 
187: Sentry captures:
188: - Unhandled exceptions in HTTP requests (via `Sentry.PlugContext`)
189: - Failed Oban jobs (via Oban integration)
190: - `Logger.error/1` calls and process crashes (via `Sentry.LoggerHandler`)
191: - Oban cron check-ins (optional, for cron monitoring)
192: 
193: ### Fly.io deployment (Phoenix API)
194: 
195: Phoenix deploys to Fly.io as an Elixir release built by `apps/phoenix/Dockerfile`, with `fly.toml` at the repo root.
196: 
197: ```bash
198: # Required locally/CI: flyctl and FLY_API_TOKEN
199: mise run phx-fly-deploy        # fly deploy --depot (Fly Depot builder, persistent org-scoped layer cache)
200: ```
201: 
202: The container runs Phoenix through `fnox exec --profile production -- /app/bin/dhc start`, and the Fly release command runs migrations through the same fnox profile. `fnox.toml` uses the `production` profile and 1Password vault `Production-phoenix-api`. Create one 1Password item per runtime env var (for example `DATABASE_URL`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`) with the value in the item's password field.
203: 
204: The only runtime bootstrap secret stored in Fly should be `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN`, scoped to the 1Password production vault:
205: 
206: ```bash
207: fly secrets set OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN=ops_... --app dhc-dashboard
208: ```
209: 
210: Rotating app secrets in 1Password does not require `fly secrets set` or a new image; restart Machines to reload them through `fnox exec`. Only rotate the Fly secret when the 1Password service account token itself changes.
211: 
212: GitHub Actions workflow: `.github/workflows/deploy-phoenix-fly.yml`. Required GitHub secret: `FLY_API_TOKEN`. Optional GitHub variable: `FLY_PHOENIX_APP` (defaults to `dhc-dashboard`).
213: 
214: The workflow builds with `flyctl deploy --depot` (Fly's Depot builder), which provides persistent org-scoped Docker layer caching across builds. This is faster and more deterministic than `--remote-only`'s pooled builder, which may hand you a cold VM with no cache. The mise toolchain is installed inside the Dockerfile during the remote build, so the workflow does not install mise on the GitHub runner.
215: 
216: ## API Contract (full pipeline)
217: 
218: Regenerate **both** sides of the API contract — Phoenix controller stubs and TypeScript client — in one step:
219: 
220: ```bash
221: mise run api-gen
222: ```
223: 
224: Fails fast: if either step exits non-zero, mise stops immediately and does not proceed.
225: 
226: **`mix gen.controllers` clobber caveat**: the task maps every operation under a tag to a REST action derived from HTTP method + path (or `operationId`), and regenerates the *whole* controller + JSON renderer + contract test for that tag. When a tag carries multiple non-REST operations (e.g. `Members` has `members.list`, `members.analytics`, `members.insuranceForm`), `--force=<path>` will overwrite the controller with stubs that map *all three* to `index` and call a non-existent `Members.list_members()` — clobbering any hand-written action bodies. After regenerating, restore the hand-written controller (keep your real action names + bodies) and never re-run `--force` on a tag whose controller you've fleshed out unless you're prepared to restore it from git. The JSON renderer and contract test are likewise tag-scoped, so extend them by hand for non-REST operations.
227: 
228: ## API Client (TypeScript)
229: 
230: ```bash
231: # Generate client from OpenAPI spec (from project root)
232: mise run api-gen
233: 
234: # Or run just the TS side
235: pnpm api-gen
236: 
237: # Watch mode (regenerate on spec changes)
238: pnpm --filter @dhc/api-client api:generate:watch
239: ```
240: 
241: Generated output: `packages/api-client/src/client/` (gitignored — auto-regenerated on `pnpm install` via postinstall, do not manually edit)
242: 
243: **Manual step after `mise run api-gen`**: `packages/api-client/src/index.ts` is hand-maintained (tracked, not generated). `openapi-ts` only writes to `src/client/`; it does not update the public re-exports in `src/index.ts`. After adding a new operation, manually add the generated SDK function plus its `types.gen` / `valibot.gen` / `@tanstack/svelte-query.gen` exports to the four `export` blocks in `src/index.ts` (mirror how `waitlistStatus` / `membersInsuranceForm` are exposed). Without this, the function exists in `src/client/` but is not importable from `@dhc/api-client`.
244: 
245: `packages/api-client/openapi-ts.config.ts` explicitly points `output.tsConfigPath` at `packages/api-client/tsconfig.json` so postinstall generation works in deployment environments that do not expose the repo-root SvelteKit `tsconfig.json`.
246: 
247: `@hey-api/openapi-ts` + Valibot currently emits invalid TypeScript for boolean schemas expressed as `enum: [true]`/`enum: [false]` (it generates `v.picklist([true])`, but Valibot picklists are typed for string/number/bigint). For response flags that are always true on success, use `type: boolean` plus a description instead of a single-value boolean enum.
248: 
249: Usage in SvelteKit:
250: ```ts
251: import { configureClient, healthIndex } from '@dhc/api-client';
252: 
253: // Configure once at app startup (e.g., +layout.svelte or hooks)
254: configureClient({
255:   baseUrl: 'http://localhost:4000/api',
256:   getAuthToken: async () => {
257:     const { data } = await supabase.auth.getSession();
258:     return data.session?.access_token;
259:   },
260: });
261: 
262: // Then use SDK functions
263: const { data, error } = await healthIndex();
264: ```
265: 
266: ## Stripe API Client (Elixir, generated)
267: 
268: ```bash
269: # Regenerate from Stripe OpenAPI spec (downloads spec, trims, generates)
270: mise run stripe-gen
271: ```
272: 
273: Generated output: `apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/stripe/generated/` (committed so production builds do not need to regenerate it; do not manually edit).
274: 
275: To add new Stripe endpoints:
276: 1. Add the operation ID to `@allowed_operations` in `apps/phoenix/lib/mix/tasks/stripe.gen.ex`
277: 2. Also add it to `@allowed_operations` in `apps/phoenix/dev/dhc/stripe/processor.ex` (the oapi_generator filter)
278: 3. Run `mise run stripe-gen` (or `cd apps/phoenix && MIX_ENV=dev mix stripe.gen`)
279: 4. Commit the regenerated output in `apps/phoenix/lib/dhc/stripe/generated/`
280: 5. Use the generated functions via `Dhc.Stripe.Operations.*` with `Dhc.Stripe.Client`
281: 
282: - Do not hand-roll Stripe endpoint calls with `Dhc.Stripe.Client.request/1` in domain code. If an endpoint exists in Stripe's OpenAPI spec, find the operation ID by the Stripe URL, add that exact ID to both allow-lists above, regenerate, and call the generated `Dhc.Stripe.Operations.*` function. If generation still fails after both allow-lists match the current spec, debug the generator/filter rather than bypassing it.
283: 
284: Hand-written modules: `Dhc.Stripe.Client` (Req adapter), `Dhc.Stripe.Processor` (allowlist filter), `Dhc.StripeSync` (sync business logic), `Dhc.StripeSync.Worker` (Oban worker).
285: 
286: The Stripe API version is pinned in app config (`:stripe_api_version`, default `"2025-10-29.clover"`) and sent as the `Stripe-Version` header on every request. This matches the version used by the existing Deno edge functions (`src/lib/server/stripe.ts`). When updating, change the config value in all three env configs (`config.exs`, `dev.exs`, `test.exs`, `runtime.exs`), update `src/lib/server/stripe.ts`, and re-run `mise run stripe-gen`.

288: ## Seeds
289: 
290: ```bash
291: # Phoenix Mix tasks replacing legacy scripts/seed*.js
292: mise run seed-waitlist
293: mise run seed-waitlist 50
294: mise run seed-invitations
295: mise run seed-invitations 50
296: mise run seed-members
297: mise run seed-members 25
298: mise run seed-committee
299: mise run seed-committee ./scripts/users.csv
300: 
301: # Or run directly from Phoenix app
302: cd apps/phoenix && mix seed.waitlist 50
303: cd apps/phoenix && mix seed.invitations 50
304: cd apps/phoenix && mix seed.members 25
305: cd apps/phoenix && mix seed.committee_members ../../scripts/users.csv
306: ```
307: 
308: `mise` loads `.env` automatically; the seed Mix tasks do not load dotenv themselves. Keep `.env` up to date with the same Phoenix DB connection convention used by the app (`DATABASE_URL`, preferred). `seed.members`, `seed.workshops`, and `seed.committee_members` create Phoenix Principals directly through `Dhc.Auth`. `seed.invitations` creates direct, pending member invitations without a waitlist entry or an issuing administrator. `seed.members` only creates Stripe customers when `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` is set. The committee CSV is intentionally local and gitignored because it contains member data; pass its path explicitly when `scripts/users.csv` is not present.

313: mise run ci                 # lint + format-check + type-check + unit tests

# @dhc/email-templates

Code-authored transactional email templates (ADR 0022). Each Email Kind is a
React Email component in `emails/` whose file also declares its metadata —
default subject, default sender, declared variables — via `defineTemplate`,
making TypeScript the single schema authority for what each Kind requires.

The five whitelisted kinds mirror `@transactional_ids` in `Dhc.Email.Worker`:
`inviteMember`, `workshopAnnouncement`, `workshopRegistration`,
`workshopRegistrationError`, `magicLink`.

## How templates reach Resend

Templates are **hosted at Resend** and addressed at send time by a stable
alias: the kebab-case of the Email Kind (`magicLink` → `magic-link`). The sync
pipeline renders every component to HTML and upserts it by that alias through
the official Resend SDK's Templates API. Rerunning is idempotent.

```bash
pnpm --filter @dhc/email-templates sync            # upsert drafts (what CI runs on PRs)
pnpm --filter @dhc/email-templates sync:publish    # upsert + publish   (what CI runs on main)
pnpm --filter @dhc/email-templates smoke           # fail unless every kind has a published template
```

Both write modes require a **Full Access** API key in `RESEND_API_KEY`
(CI secret `RESEND_API_KEY_CI`); send-only keys cannot manage templates.
`EMAIL_ASSETS_BASE_URL` overrides where `/static/…` asset sources are
rewritten to (defaults to `https://dashboard.dublinhemaclub.com`; the crest
itself ships as `apps/web/static/logo.png`).

Rendered HTML keeps literal `{{{VARIABLE}}}` markers — the render props are
placeholders, never sample data — so Resend substitutes real values at send
time. Variables are declared on the template even when the markup does not
render them.

## CI wiring

`.github/workflows/email-templates.yml` gates like every other pipeline: a
change-detection job (`dorny/paths-filter`) skips everything unless
`packages/email-templates/**` (or workspace lockfiles / the workflow itself)
changed; lint, typecheck and tests run first.

- **Pull requests upload drafts only.** Nothing on Resend changes publicly
  until merge.
- **Merging to main publishes**, then smoke-checks that all five aliases
  resolve to published templates. Publishing therefore gates on review plus
  required checks — never an arbitrary push.

Make **Email Templates / Sync templates to Resend** a required status check so
unreviewed template changes cannot reach `main`.

## Drift policy

**The repository is the source of truth for template content; the next sync
overwrites any dashboard edit.** Editing a template in Resend's dashboard is
drift: it survives only until someone touches the corresponding component and
syncs again. There is no import-back flow.

Recovery for bad publishes is **Resend's version history**: every publish is a
new version, so roll back from the dashboard rather than editing content
there. If you do hot-fix in the dashboard during an incident, port the change
into the component in the same PR that follows the incident — otherwise the
next sync silently reverts it.

## Local preview

```bash
pnpm --filter @dhc/email-templates dev   # React Email preview server on :3000
```

The preview server serves `emails/static/` for relative assets; production
renders get their assets rewritten to absolute club-site URLs by the sync
(relative image sources break in email clients).
